3. Tolerances 

3.1 Tolerance on taper on gauge diameter d ■» ± IT6. 

3.2 Tolerances ort dimensions without specified tolerances shall be of grade ' medium ' according to 
IS : 2102-1969 ' Allowable deviations for dimensions without specified tolerances ( first revision ) \ 



APPENDIX A 

METHOD OF MEASURING TOLERANCE ON TAPERS 

A-1. Measuring Instruments— It is recommended that for the inspection of tapers, the diameters 
should be measured with the help of optical measuring instruments or by the method of comparison 
with master gauges on comparators. 

A-2. Method off Measuring — The diameter at any point B is measured at the small end of the taper. 
With the help of this diameter and the basic ratio of taper, the diameter at point C at a distance AC is 
calculated. The measured diameter at C shall not deviate from the calculated values of diameter at C by 
more than the values given below: 

7124 Taper Number Permissible Deviation 




30 
40 
45 
50 
55 
60

A-3. Inspection — The taper shanks and sockets shall be inspected by the method of taking bearing. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was originally published in 1964 based on the draft ISO Recommendation 
No. 389 issued by the International Organization for Standardization. The revision of IS : 2340*1964 
was necessitated to bring in. line with the recent work done at international ( ISO ) level. The present 
version which covers only dimensions for arbor and tool shanks, has been enlarged to include dimen- 
sions for 7/24 taper No. 45, 55, 65, 70, 75 and 80. The dimensions for collars have been included. 

The dimensions for 7/24 tapers for spindle noses are covered in IS : 6681-1972 ' Dimensions for 
self-release 7/24 tapers for spindle noses for milling machines '. 



This standard conforms to ISO/R 297 and ISO/R 297/Amendment 1.

Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
